title: multi-sdk: synchronize auth + retry defaults, stabilize streaming ergonomics, bump SDK versions
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: SDK users across Python/TypeScript/Go reported subtle differences in auth token refresh timing, retry backoff defaults, and streaming client ergonomics which caused production surprises (duplicate reconnects, inconsistent transient error handling, and awkward streaming iterator APIs). This PR harmonizes defaults and adds ergonomic helpers so apps have consistent behavior across languages.

What this PR does (high level):
- Unifies auth token refresh window to 60s before expiry across all SDKs and centralizes the refresh retry loop to avoid double-refresh races.
- Introduces a shared exponential+jitter retry policy reference and applies it to request-level retries (idempotent endpoints) and streaming reconnection backoff. Default: initial=200ms, factor=2.0, max=8s, jitter=0.25.
- Stabilizes streaming APIs: Python iterator now yields a StreamChunk object with .delta/.done fields; TypeScript streaming helper exposes both async iterable() and event-emitter patterns; Go adds a StreamReader helper with CloseWithError semantics.
- Adds ergonomic helpers: client.with_retry_policy(...) factory, client.stream(context, opts) convenience overloads, and language-native examples in /examples/sdks.
- Bumps SDK package versions: python 1.8.0, typescript 0.9.2, go 0.7.1 and updates changelogs.
- Tests: integration tests for token refresh race, streaming reconnects under transient network faults, and retry-herd mitigation.

Notes on scope: The changes are implemented inside the sdk/ subpackages (python/, typescript/, go/) in the monorepo; no server changes required. The PR is intentionally focused on defaults and ergonomics — no breaking API surface changes for existing callers, only additive helpers and safer defaults.

Checklist:
- [x] Central retry policy implemented and used by all SDKs
- [x] Auth refresh window unified and race conditions addressed
- [x] Streaming ergonomic helpers added for Python/TS/Go
- [x] Unit + integration tests added and passing
- [x] Changelogs and version bumps for packaging

Related work: Linear: ENG-4219, ENG-4278; follow-up: ENG-4350 (doc examples & migration guide).

Files changed summary (high level):
- sdk/python/redwood/client.py: central retry decorator, TokenRefresher class, StreamChunk type, new examples
- sdk/python/tests/test_streaming_reconnect.py: flaky network simulation tests
- sdk/typescript/src/retry.ts: new ExponentialJitterPolicy and applyRetry middleware
- sdk/typescript/src/streaming.ts: added AsyncIterable + EventEmitter shim
- sdk/go/client/retry.go: RetryPolicy struct and helper functions
- sdk/go/stream/reader.go: StreamReader helper and examples
- sdk/*/CHANGELOG.md and package version files updated

Commit summary: 
- Add central retry policy (python/ts/go)
- Implement TokenRefresher with single-flight semantics in Python
- Streaming ergonomics: iterator/emitter/readers
- Tests for reconnect and retry behaviours
- Bump versions and update changelogs

CI and checks: overall CI passed after second run. One flaky streaming test in CI initially failed (network simulator timeout); test fixture adjusted to be more deterministic and rerun green. All packages built and wheel/npm/go modules published to internal staging registry as part of the release job.

Merge: Squash and merge to main. See merge commit details for combined changelog entries.

Additional context for reviewers: This is a cross-language change so please pay attention to parity of defaults and the semantics described in the in-repo docs (sdk/README.md). If you maintain downstream SDK packages, the version bumps are non-breaking but consumers relying on previous retry windows may observe fewer auth refresh failures.

review_conversation: Marcus Li: Left a comment about the single-flight token refresher — can we use an existing singleflight util rather than rolling our own?

Asha Patel: Replied that we evaluated the internal util; it had lifecycle constraints in Python (async vs sync) so I implemented a small single-flight shim local to the TokenRefresher and added tests covering race conditions.
Sofia Gonzales: Requested that the TS streaming helper expose both AsyncIterable and an on('data') style API for parity with existing consumer code. Added shim in streaming.ts.
Evan Park: Noted linter warnings for gofmt and small nil-check in StreamReader; pushed follow-up commit to address both and added unit.
Marcus Li: Approved after test fixes and a minor comment on changelog phrasing.
release_notes:
- SDK: unify auth refresh timing and token refresh race mitigation across Python/TS/Go
- SDK: introduce shared exponential+jitter retry defaults (safer reconnects)
- SDK: improve streaming ergonomics (Python StreamChunk, TS AsyncIterable+EventEmitter, Go StreamReader)
- SDK: bump package versions (python 1.8.0, typescript 0.9.2, go 0.7.1)
notes_for_release_manager: Publish jobs are in ci/publish-sdks.yml and push artifacts to internal staging. After publish, verify example projects in examples/sdks with new SDK versions and update public docs if release notes need expansion (ENG-4350).
testing_summary: Added unit tests for retry policy, integration tests for streaming reconnect and auth refresh races. Local stress runs indicated a 3x reduction in observed duplicate refresh attempts under bursty traffic. CI shows flakiness resolved after fixture timeout adjustment.
security_review: No new permissions or secrets. Token refresh uses existing KMS-wrapped credentials. Security reviewed the single-flight shim to ensure it does not hold sensitive tokens beyond intended lifetime.
user_impact: Low friction for existing users; improved stability under network error conditions. Consumers wanting previous aggressive retry behaviour can override client.with_retry_policy().
migration_guidance: No breaking changes. If you implemented custom streaming parsers, switch to new StreamChunk or adjust to the AsyncIterable API; migration examples added to sdk/examples/migration.md.
